scenario: A btrfs mount whose device basename is listed under two different uuids under /sys/fs/btrfs, so the device-to-filesystem mapping is ambiguous and the quota state is unknown rather than enabled or disabled.

fixture.mountinfo:
23 28 0:21 / /proc rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:12 - proc proc rw
24 1 0:30 /@root / rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/dm-0 rw,compress=zstd:3,ssd,discard=async,space_cache=v2,subvolid=256,subvol=/@root
30 28 259:1 / /tmp rw,relatime shared:1 - xfs /dev/nvme0n1p1 rw,inode64,logbufs=8,logbsize=256k,noquota
36 28 0:44 /@data /srv/data rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/dm-3 rw,compress=zstd:3,ssd,discard=async,space_cache=v2,subvolid=257,subvol=/@data

rationale: Contract section C2, quota-classification table, the btrfs row 'zero or several uuids list the device' -> unknown / n/a / btrfs_device_unmapped, unchanged by the round-23 pre-seal amendment, which states only that 'Zero/multiple UUID matches remains unknown' and does not re-tokenise that basis. This fixture places the device basename dm-3 in the devices list of TWO uuids (a7c3e9d1-4f62-4b8e-9d21-5c7f0a3b6e11 and f2b5d804-7c19-4e62-8a3d-91b0e5c7d2a4), so neither 'exactly one uuid' row can apply and the several-claimants row governs: quota_state unknown, enforcement n/a, basis btrfs_device_unmapped. The two claimants deliberately AGREE on qgroups (both present, both qgroups_enabled true, mode 'qgroup') so that the expectation 'unknown' holds under every reading of the exactly-one rows: no reading of 'exactly one uuid whose qgroups is true' is satisfied by two claimants, and no reading of 'exactly one uuid, qgroups false' is satisfied either; the case therefore isolates the several-claimants condition alone, and an implementation that resolves the device by taking the first, the last, or any single matching uuid lands on 'enabled' and is caught. Per the amendment, fixture source resolution looks up the RAW decoded source in device_links and uses its mapped basename when present, otherwise basename(source): the raw source is /dev/dm-3, device_links maps it to dm-3, and dm-3 is compared against every uuid devices list, which yields two matches and therefore unknown. Per the amendment, qgroups directory presence means INITIALIZED, not enabled, so each uuid record now carries the required qgroups_enabled member: the two claimants are qgroups true with qgroups_enabled true (the enabled state, which the claimant rows would report as btrfs_qgroups_enabled if the mapping were unambiguous, but here the ambiguity preempts it), and the decoy on the other device is qgroups false paired with qgroups_enabled null and mode null as the amendment requires. Mount resolution follows the contract rule 'candidate mounts: mount point equals realpath, or is /, or realpath starts with mount point + /; choose the longest mount point' read over the proc.rst section 3.5 field layout (S082, Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst:1965-1990: fields 1-6, optional fields until the '-' separator, then filesystem type, mount source, super options): for realpath /srv/data/store the candidates are '/' (the /@root btrfs line) and '/srv/data' (the /@data btrfs line, since /srv/data/store starts with '/srv/data/'); the longest wins, so mount_point is /srv/data, fstype btrfs, mount source /dev/dm-3, and the '/' candidate is not selected. No covering mount point occurs twice, so the amendment's ambiguous_overmount refusal does not apply; the trailing empty line is ignored per the amendment. Device check: fstype is btrfs and the path st_dev 0:57 has stat major 0, so the amendment's rule 'Btrfs skips equality only when stat major is 0' skips the equality check and the btrfs mismatch is not a device_mismatch verdict; per S081 (fs/btrfs/inode.c, btrfs_getattr:8215-8218 and 'stat->dev = BTRFS_I(inode)->root->anon_dev' at 8246) a btrfs path reports the subvolume's anonymous device number, so the mismatch is expected, and the path proceeds to quota classification. The frozen real control frozen/c2-expected-real.json corroborates this reading: its btrfs fleet root (mount 0:30, st_dev 0:57, stat major 0) carries basis btrfs_qgroups_dir_absent, not device_mismatch. S079 (fs/btrfs/sysfs.c) supports the fixture's device-mapping shape: the per-fsid 'devices' kobject is created under /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid>/devices (fs_devs->devices_kobj = kobject_create_and_add("devices", ...), sysfs.c:2266) and btrfs_sysfs_add_device links each block device into it by the block device's own kernel name (sysfs_create_link(devices_kobj, disk_kobj, disk_kobj->name), sysfs.c:2155), which is the name the contract calls the device basename; the same file shows the 'qgroups' group under /sys/fs/btrfs/<uuid>/qgroups/ with its 'enabled' and 'mode' attributes (qgroup_enabled_show at 2355, qgroup_mode_show at 2370, the qgroups attribute group and its path comment at 2450-2461) that the fixture's qgroups / qgroups_enabled / qgroups_mode fields mirror, and qgroup_mode_show emits exactly 'qgroup' (BTRFS_QGROUP_MODE_FULL) or 'squota' (BTRFS_QGROUP_MODE_SIMPLE), so 'qgroup' is a legal mode text. S080 (fs/btrfs/qgroup.c) supports the meaning of the qgroups flag: btrfs_sysfs_add_qgroups creates that group when qgroups are initialised (qgroup.c:441 and :1032) and btrfs_sysfs_del_qgroups destroys it (qgroup.c:620, :689, :1295), so qgroups false means the group is absent for that filesystem. Verdict precedence: the fixture is well formed (no setup error), no path is enabled, the single path is unknown, therefore exit 2 and finding_id QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN.
